title: THE GATEKEEPER SHE FINISHED THE SENTENCES OF
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: This is the corrected set's clearest new dramatic engine: Illuminara's formidable speed becomes the obstacle without making her weak, while Halvard's tacit craft, Runa's engineering judgment and the approaching surge create a concrete test that dialogue alone cannot satisfy. The love-direction is embodied in restraint, patient listening and preserved authorship, and the local scale gives the day an immediate human opening.

R14 check before prose. Aim: the tide-gate holds against the surge, nine thousand people stay dry, and the one man who knows the gate is not made redundant by being rescued. Counterpart: Halvard Beck (79; wants to be asked, not to be right; his tacit craft has never been written down because nobody waited for the end of his sentences), Runa Beck (engineer; drew the array so he would never climb the ladder in a storm, and heard her own love read as a headstone), Idun Maas (chair; legitimate duty to nine thousand, will not hang the town on one visitor or one old man). Strongest objection on the page: Maas in scene 2 and again in scene 5 (two-for-two is not a law; she will remember tonight as the night they were lucky), and Runa's refusal to pretend the array can learn the seat in a day. What Illuminara must understand: her speed is the obstacle; the missing variable is not only a fact (a tongue of silt under the left seat) but a timing (the water leans the foot down and packs it) that her force sense, which reads what pushes and not when, would not have reached. Love in action: she says plainly what she did, sits on the step all night with no correction, asks one question per hour or so, holds the sentence she already has (the coin in her mouth), and then carries only the cracked bearing and touches nothing else. Freely chosen change: Halvard opens the bolt at 04:30, makes two time-bound predictions, authorises the writing and signs Maas's order; Maas keeps her own fallback (the dike, a 22:10 deadline); Runa turns the left wheel on his word. A vivid, unusually disciplined draft. Illuminara's over-fast understanding creates a real mistake without making her incompetent; Halvard's two predictions are written before measurement, Runa supplies independent instrumentation and Maas retains authority. The held sentence is love expressed as costly restraint, and the gate, compensation, shared manual and conditional trust make the result concrete. Three causal improvements remain: Halvard's deepest objection is inferred rather than spoken, Maas's fallback does not yet visibly protect all nine thousand people if the gate stays open, and the ending still leaves the future system dependent on 'the man who hears it' without proving Runa can inherit the signal.

Revision of T01 answering GPT's T02 review (REVISE_BEFORE_FINAL). Everything the critic asked to protect is kept: the three right readings and the wrong one, the plain admission, the coin held in the mouth, Halvard's answer going one step beyond hers, the two signed predictions tested against rod and tuner, Maas's signature requirement and refusal of permanent dependence, the day-one cost and the conditional trust. Changes are local: one spoken objection in scene 3, a life-safe fallback and its cost in scene 5 with its echo in scene 6, and a first verified transfer of knowledge in scenes 6 and 7. Power decides nothing between beings; Illuminara's one physical act remains carrying the diagnosed bearing. Outcome: gate holds, nine thousand safe, Fisher's Row compensated, Halvard credited and no longer the sole interpreter, with trust returning as a rule.

T03 fully answers the three causal requests without losing the draft's restraint. Halvard now states the wound in his own cadence and Illuminara answers by not explaining him to himself; Maas's abort branch protects every life at a real, named cost; Runa proves one bounded transfer of craft and the manual makes succession testable. The gate still holds because evidence, consent, Halvard's knowledge, Runa's engineering and Illuminara's limited physical help work together. One local numerical contradiction should be corrected before final: Halvard says she was right four times while the deck and Illuminara's admission establish three right readings and one damaging mistake.

Final. GPT's T04 review found T03 ready for final after one local continuity correction, and that is the only prose change: Halvard's line in The Step now reads 'Three times you were right, and the one time you weren't it sounded the same', matching the deck, Illuminara's own admission and the scene-one sequence (three right readings, one damaging wrong one). Everything the critic asked to protect is untouched: his spoken objection and its two-line cadence, her withheld answer and the coin in the mouth, the life-safe Salt Meadow fallback, Runa's independent call, the three-note certification rule, the bounded bearing and the conditional rule at breakfast. Outcome unchanged: gate holds, nine thousand safe, Fisher's Row compensated, the method credited to both Becks and now teachable, trust returning as a rule.

final_critic_line: Illuminara repairs the harm of finishing Halvard's sentences by learning to wait for the knowledge her force-sense cannot supply; Halvard, Runa and Maas each retain authority, the gate holds under a measured and life-safe plan, and the craft becomes teachable without erasing its first keeper.
